summary: Guest-to-staff Okta profile conversion causes department claim loss and console RBAC deny
description:
Issue summary:
A newly converted employee (previously a guest account) cannot access the internal Runbooks and Model Insights consoles. Okta profile shows successful conversion from guest to staff, but the 'department' attribute is missing in the SCIM snapshot causing RBAC role mapping to evaluate to null.

Impact:
- One user blocked from internal tools used by SRE and Platform (Runbooks, Model Insights).
- Potentially affects other recently converted guests (we have 6 conversion events in the last 24h in the same org unit).
- Not a company-wide outage but blocks oncall and developer workflows in a handful of teams.

Environment:
- Production (us-east Okta org).
- Affected user: user@example.com (converted guest account, employee ID 8642).
- Console versions: web-console v3.14.1, identity-proxy v2.7.0.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) OKTA: Admin console shows guest -> staff status change at 2026-03-12T08:14:23Z.
2) SCIM-provisioner log shows PATCH provisioning event to internal identity service at 2026-03-12T08:14:30Z.
3) Identity service consumed SCIM patch but department attribute is absent in the payload.
4) RBAC mapping rule for Runbooks requires department non-empty; evaluation returns no roles and console returns 403.

Expected behavior:
- After guest->staff conversion, SCIM should include department (or fallback group mapping) and roles should be granted per RBAC rules.

Observed logs (see logs_snippets field for excerpts).

Workaround:
- Manual SCIM patch via Admin -> Users to add department attribute. This allowed immediate access.

Notes:
- Customer-facing support not involved (internal ticket).
- Suspect race between Okta attribute update and SCIM user object canonicalization for guest identities.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Convert a guest account to staff in Okta admin.
2. Observe SCIM provisioning events and payloads in identity-provisioner logs.
3. Confirm console role mapping and 403 on web-console for the converted user.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:05 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after internal engineer reported 403 when opening Runbooks. Provided Okta event id: 0oab12345EXAMPLE.
2026-03-12 09:30 - Arjun Patel: Assigned and started triage. Requested SCIM provisioning logs and a full company-org snapshot for the affected user.
2026-03-12 10:12 - SRE (Liam O'Rourke): Found 6 similar provisioning events in the last 24h from the same org unit; attaching log excerpt to investigation notes.

2026-03-12 11:00 - Identity team (Priya Singh): Noted that guest identities use a different canonical ID and that the SCIM mapper had a conditional that skipped department when metadata.source=="guest". Investigating intended behavior.
2026-03-12 13:40 - Arjun Patel: Applied manual SCIM patch adding 'department' to the user's identity record. User confirmed access restored. Planning rollback-safe fix and unit tests for SCIM mapper.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: SCIM mapper logic intentionally excluded department for guest -> historical behavior. Conditional recently changed in deploy v2.7.0 and now incorrectly persists 'source==guest' for converted accounts.
Hypothesis 2: Race condition where Okta profile attribute write and group sync operations occur in separate events; provisioning consumer sees an intermediate state lacking department.

Evidence: SCIM provisioning payloads (see logs_snippets) show two consecutive events: an initial 'status_change' with minimal attrs, and a follow-up 'profile_update' that includes department ~3s later. Our consumer dedup logic ignores the second event if the canonical ID differs.

Investigation step: Replayed provisioning events in staging using the same ordering; observed consumer dropped the profile_update due to a canonical_id mismatch for guest-derived accounts. Root cause points to identity canonicalization algorithm not unifying guest->staff IDs until after first event processing.
Slack threads: #identity-sync thread ts: 2026-03-12T09:15 in #identity-sync (link: slack.com/archives/C12345/p164...)
logs_snippets: [2026-03-12T08:14:33Z] identity-consumer WARN Dropping event for 00u1abcd1234: canonical_id mismatch (guest:00u1abcd1234 != staff:uid-9876).
workaround: Manual SCIM patch was applied by Identity team to add 'department'. For now, runbook: identity-admins can patch affected users in Admin -> Users. Staging repro available for validation.
resolution: In Progress - planned fix: update identity canonicalization to unify guest->staff identifiers prior to event dedup, and make SCIM mapper idempotent for transient 'source' values. Patch scheduled for canary on 2026-03-15. Post-deploy tasks: add unit/integration tests and a diagnostic metric for dropped provisioning events.
postmortem_followups: 1) Fix identity canonicalization logic and deploy to canary (owner: identity team).
2) Add integration test covering guest->staff conversion event ordering (owner: identity-team/integration-tests).
3) Create alert when scim consumer drops >0 events/min for a given org unit (owner: SRE).
4) Update runbook with explicit troubleshooting steps for guest conversions (owner: ops-docs).
notes: Ticket created to capture internal access regression affecting guest conversions. Will update after canary results.
